record.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:92 — Read-then-write is not transactional; two concurrent requests adding the same email both pass the uniqueness filter and both insert

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the code reads current attendees (prisma.booking.findFirst include attendees) and computes `uniqueGuests` by filtering against that snapshot, then later performs a separate `prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)`. There is no transaction or atomic upsert/unique constraint handling shown here, so two concurrent requests can both observe that an email is not yet in `booking.attendees` and both proceed to `createMany` for the same email. That creates a classic read-then-write race (either duplicates if allowed, or an unhandled DB constraint error if a unique index exists).
